summary: This is a confirmation run (iteration 5) to verify that the established k=5 BFS-optimal endgame algorithm achieves score 100/100 on the judge, matching results from iterations 3 and 4. The problem is considered solved — this arm exists only to produce a final reproducibility check before closing the campaign.
key_points: Single arm (h-main): Re-run the k=5 circular-buffer rotation sort that places elements 1 through n−5 using ≤2 operations each, then solves the last 5 elements via a 119-case BFS lookup table. Expected operation counts per case: 1982–1990 (avg 1986), well below the 2001 threshold needed for score 100.

Confirmation criterion: Score = 100 and per-case operation counts identical to iteration 4's values [1987, 1987, 1983, 1987, 1990, 1984, 1982, 1990, 1987, 1983]. Any deviation would indicate a test-data change or code regression, not an algorithmic issue.

No additional arms are included because the score ceiling (100) is algebraically guaranteed for any algorithm using ≤2001 ops per n=1000 case, ablation and dose-response dimensions are exhausted (confirmed in iters 2–4), and all 10 test cases share n=1000 so no regime variation exists to probe.

Refutation condition: If score < 100 or operation counts differ from prediction, diagnose by checking compiler flags, solution.cpp version (should contain 119 endgame branches), and whether test data has changed. This would trigger a new investigation iteration rather than invalidating the algorithm.
Recommendation: Approve if the goal is a clean final confirmation; alternatively, skip this iteration and close the campaign, since iterations 3 and 4 already achieved score 100 with identical code.
